content.text: I've e-mailed Fedora committer list.
+1 to disabling this behavior.
Would it be possible for you to provide a minimal example of such a request so that I can make sure we're on the same page and create an IT to gauge the impact of disabling this behavior? Thanks.
Yes, but not until next week.
can you make me a subtask for this?
are you going to working on this this week?
Here's an example of a "bad" request:
PUT to /some/resource:
</some/resource> <info:rubydora#label> "a label".
</some/other/Location> <info:rubydora#label> "some other label".
The second triple should cause the request to throw a 403. Without that second triple, the request would be fine.
, do you anticipate having time this week for this ticket?
Not sure right now how to tackle this. It seems that whenever a HTTP-supplied body stream is converted into a Model, it gets populated with F4 subjects (along with the target resource). I'm using:
model.listSubjects()

So, I'm not sure how to distinguish between a non-target resource and a valid subject in the Model. It can definitely be checked if a subject is a F4 subject, but what if there are other legit subjects in the model?
The only valid subject would be the one that is created from the request target, right? All others are invalid, if I understand the ticket correctly.
"created
or updated
from the request target", yes.
Ok, I think I understand now.
No, I meant that the RDF subject was
constructed
syntactically
, from the request target. The question of create vs. update doesn't obtain here. The thing that is created is an URI, not any persistent thing.
There are a few unit tests such as the following in FedoraLdpIT:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/b94778562793ea0163a6f7aeab66d6544766b08b/fcrepo-http-api/src/test/java/org/fcrepo/integration/http/api/FedoraLdpIT.java#L780
that land subjects like the following in a Model:
[code]
[code]
So, it doesn't seem to be possible to distinguish between legit subjects when a GET is made before PUT. The ajs6f test are ok because there the Model only contains triples without the F4 namespace.
So,
(I) it seems that the tests will need to be re-written or adorned with @Ignore.

(2) for @Patch, the requestBody (application/sparql-update) cannot be converted into a Model. We would have to rely on getting subjects by using a regex and having the validation logic in FedoraLdp (not the kernel). Not sure if this is good approach.
Are you okay with 1 and 2?
I'm confused,
. Why is it not possible to distinguish between a triple-subject that was created from the target of the request and something like "
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml
", which is quite obviously not the target of any request?
The test illustrates that (around 790).
In your new IT test that there are two resources, A and B. So, when it's easy to see that when a request is made to A, B is the unwanted resource.

But in the cited test case, the update request contains A and F4 subjects when the Model is obtained in ContentExposingResource or FedoraResourceImpl. So, it doesn't seem possible to say that F4 is okay but B is not, when looking at the Model.
A = a JCR node
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml

I understand your objection even less now. Looking at that test, to distinguish the two kinds of triples seems even easier: those with `subjectURI` as subject are okay, all others are not. What do you mean by "A" and "F4"?
I've pushed up a test branch that highlights the logging output difference for the following two tests:
For the test that now passes OK:
testCreateGraphWithNonLocalTriples()

Please either move your branch to the main (shared) repository or give me rights to comment on your branch.
I added you as a collaborator. Thanks.
Thanks. Can you make a PR now from that branch, so that I can give line-attached comments?
I created a PR against fcrepo.
I hate to say it, but I
still
don't see the problem (other than the bad logic I noted in the PR). The logging you show looks fine to me. Changes
do

need to be made to the round-trip test. Obviously, we don't expect to do a round-trip without filtering under the "new regime". But I do not understand why writing that filter seems to present a problem. Just select (from the results of the GET) the triples with subject the same as the request target and use those for the PUT.
For some reason Prefer header doesn't seem to be doing the trick for F4 namespace triples. I thought I'd check here before stepping into the debugger.
$ curl -i -H "Prefer: return=representation; omit=\"http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml\";" http://localhost:8080/rest/enrique
Result (notice the last line in the output):

I feel a bit weird about that last triple that you're pointing to here. I can't understand what its meaning really is or exactly how (or why) we are generating it. Do you know how it arises in the RDF-generation processes? I don't think it has anything to do with namespaces: the subject "
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml
" seems a bit weird, too. In short, I'm wondering whether you have discovered a bug in RDF generation...
Also, I don't see that the subject there dereferences into anything in the legitimate repository namespace/ontology.
It's "expanding" from the "
http://localhost:8080/.../fcr:export?jcr/xml
"  perhaps?
Perhaps,
, and that is the only other place I see that "jcr/xml" string occurring, but how and why? Why would we be generating labeling triples anyway...?

"If these subjects are skolemized blank nodes, then we need to shift the locations of skolemization and your new test on the subjects with respect to each other so that the new test encounters blank nodes before they are skolemized."
Does this mean that some additional PR would be needed before the above-mentioned tests can pass?

I'm still not sure we want them to pass in their current form. Assuming that the failures are entirely due to blank nodes and we do want them to pass, and assuming that my guess above about the interaction between your new test and skolemization is right, then yes, work will be required to move your new test into a location where it encounters blank nodes before they have been skolemized. Skolemization occurs in FedoraResourceImpl and JcrPropertyStatementListener, although perhaps for your convenience you may want to move both occurrences into FedoraResourceImpl.

From the 30+ comments and feedback, and especially the last comment, it appears to me that work on this ticket is still blocked by either more future tickets or more work. It also seems to me that the side effects of a patch have not been analyzed yet. Having spent already a day or so on making a simple solution stick, and still not understanding the skolemization piece, I think I’m going to stop working on this ticket for a bit and mark it as unassigned for now.

Certainly there is more work to be done on this ticket, but not much. I think you may be overestimating what remains. Changing the qualities of "permitted" RDF is a major change to the behavior of the software, and no one should have expected this ticket to be closed in a single day.

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/6e755b2768b5a4e7496119efbcdddef1f009c163
Currently, an F4 client is able to request a PUT or PATCH on a repository resource that contains triples with other resources as their RDF subjects.
In these cases, the repository resource that is not the target of the request can be updated.
This is questionable behavior.
This task is to:
1) confirm with the F4 committer team that this behavior should be disabled
2) implement it
Note: Although this issue shows itself in the REST-API, the solution should be deeper within Fedora, i.e. within the kernel.

comments.body: I've e-mailed Fedora committer list.
+1 to disabling this behavior.

A. Soroka Would it be possible for you to provide a minimal example of such a request so that I can make sure we're on the same page and create an IT to gauge the impact of disabling this behavior? Thanks.
Yes, but not until next week.
Osman Din can you make me a subtask for this?
Osman Din are you going to working on this this week?

Here's an example of a "bad" request:

PUT to /some/resource:

</some/resource> <info:rubydora#label> "a label".
</some/other/Location> <info:rubydora#label> "some other label".

The second triple should cause the request to throw a 403. Without that second triple, the request would be fine.
Osman Din, do you anticipate having time this week for this ticket?

Not sure right now how to tackle this. It seems that whenever a HTTP-supplied body stream is converted into a Model, it gets populated with F4 subjects (along with the target resource). I'm using: 

 model.listSubjects()

So, I'm not sure how to distinguish between a non-target resource and a valid subject in the Model. It can definitely be checked if a subject is a F4 subject, but what if there are other legit subjects in the model?
The only valid subject would be the one that is created from the request target, right? All others are invalid, if I understand the ticket correctly.
"created or updated from the request target", yes.
Ok, I think I understand now.

Andrew Woods No, I meant that the RDF subject was constructed, syntactically, from the request target. The question of create vs. update doesn't obtain here. The thing that is created is an URI, not any persistent thing.

There are a few unit tests such as the following in FedoraLdpIT:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/b94778562793ea0163a6f7aeab66d6544766b08b/fcrepo-http-api/src/test/java/org/fcrepo/integration/http/api/FedoraLdpIT.java#L780

that land subjects like the following in a Model:

[code]

http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml, http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label, "jcr/xml"^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string>

[code]

So, it doesn't seem to be possible to distinguish between legit subjects when a GET is made before PUT. The ajs6f test are ok because there the Model only contains triples without the F4 namespace.

So,

(I) it seems that the tests will need to be re-written or adorned with @Ignore.

(2) for @Patch, the requestBody (application/sparql-update) cannot be converted into a Model. We would have to rely on getting subjects by using a regex and having the validation logic in FedoraLdp (not the kernel). Not sure if this is good approach.

Are you okay with 1 and 2?

I'm confused, Osman Din. Why is it not possible to distinguish between a triple-subject that was created from the target of the request and something like "http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml", which is quite obviously not the target of any request?

The test illustrates that (around 790).

In your new IT test that there are two resources, A and B. So, when it's easy to see that when a request is made to A, B is the unwanted resource.

But in the cited test case, the update request contains A and F4 subjects when the Model is obtained in ContentExposingResource or FedoraResourceImpl. So, it doesn't seem possible to say that F4 is okay but B is not, when looking at the Model.

A = a JCR node
F4 = http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml

I understand your objection even less now. Looking at that test, to distinguish the two kinds of triples seems even easier: those with `subjectURI` as subject are okay, all others are not. What do you mean by "A" and "F4"?

A. Soroka I added you as a collaborator. Thanks.
Thanks. Can you make a PR now from that branch, so that I can give line-attached comments?
I created a PR against fcrepo.

I hate to say it, but I still don't see the problem (other than the bad logic I noted in the PR). The logging you show looks fine to me. Changes do need to be made to the round-trip test. Obviously, we don't expect to do a round-trip without filtering under the "new regime". But I do not understand why writing that filter seems to present a problem. Just select (from the results of the GET) the triples with subject the same as the request target and use those for the PUT.

Osman Din I feel a bit weird about that last triple that you're pointing to here. I can't understand what its meaning really is or exactly how (or why) we are generating it. Do you know how it arises in the RDF-generation processes? I don't think it has anything to do with namespaces: the subject "http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml" seems a bit weird, too. In short, I'm wondering whether you have discovered a bug in RDF generation...
Also, I don't see that the subject there dereferences into anything in the legitimate repository namespace/ontology.
A. Soroka It's "expanding" from the "http://localhost:8080/.../fcr:export?jcr/xml" perhaps?
Perhaps, Osman Din, and that is the only other place I see that "jcr/xml" string occurring, but how and why? Why would we be generating labeling triples anyway...?

renderedFields.description:
Currently, an F4 client is able to request a PUT or PATCH on a repository resource that contains triples with other resources as their RDF subjects.
In these cases, the repository resource that is not the target of the request can be updated.
This is questionable behavior.

This task is to:
1) confirm with the F4 committer team that this behavior should be disabled
2) implement it

Note: Although this issue shows itself in the REST-API, the solution should be deeper within Fedora, i.e. within the kernel.
